why_angle: Shoppers asking for a quiet gaming controller need to know which buttons are actually silenced. The cited rivals don't say: HLPLANET's G7 page only labels face buttons 'Membrane (Quiet/Soft)', and the Reddit threads and Super Nova manual carry owner opinion or bare specs. None goes input by input through what each maker's 'quiet' covers. None quotes EasySMX's own 'tactile microswitch' D-pad wording for the X05 Pro, and none sets out that the Chitu 2 Silent Edition swaps every button and the stick rings to silicone.

page.title: Best Quiet Gaming Controller (2026): Picks for Late-Night and Shared-Room Play
page.desc: Which buttons each quiet controller actually silences: Mobapad Chitu 2 Silent, EasySMX X05 Pro, GameSir Super Nova and EasySMX S05 Pro compared by face buttons, D-pad, triggers and battery.
page.answer: Short answer. For a quiet gaming controller, the quietest is the Mobapad Chitu 2 HD Silent Edition: silicone, not microswitch, under the face buttons, D-pad, bumpers and triggers, plus silent silicone stick rings. The cheaper EasySMX X05 Pro keeps a microswitch D-pad.

page.after:
What the differences mean

  • Silenced button groups: Chitu 2 Silent 5 of 5 (ABXY, D-pad, bumpers, triggers, +/−), Super Nova 1 of 5 (ABXY). EasySMX names none for the X05 Pro or S05 Pro, so the ear tests below are what tell you.
  • Price gap: X05 Pro against Super Nova: $49.99 − $35.99 = $14.00 saved. S05 Pro against X05 Pro: $54.99 − $35.99 = $19.00 more, with a charging dock in the box.
  • Nights per charge at 2 hours a night: X05 Pro 6 ÷ 2 = 3; Chitu 2 15 ÷ 2 = 7.5; Super Nova 18 ÷ 2 = 9; S05 Pro 20 ÷ 2 = 10 (maker claim, not a test).
UseFits best
Playing beside someone asleep, Switch 2 or PCMobapad Chitu 2 HD Silent Edition
D-pad-heavy games (platformers, fighters), played quietlyChitu 2 Silent (silicone D-pad) or GameSir Super Nova (membrane D-pad)
PC or Steam Deck on the smallest budgetEasySMX X05 Pro
Switch with a charging dock includedEasySMX S05 Pro
XboxGameSir G7 SE (wired; HLPLANET lists membrane face buttons, though GameSir makes no quiet claim)
PS5Sony DualSense with vibration and trigger effects turned off (see below)

What “quiet” actually covers on each controller

Most of the noise comes from the switch under each button. EasySMX's own explainer says microswitch buttons “often produce a clear click when activated”. Rubber membranes “usually sound softer” but can still knock when the cap bottoms out. It also warns that “strong rumble can create greater room noise than the buttons”. None of these four makers publishes a decibel figure, so the comparison rests on what each maker says it silenced and on named reviewers' ear tests.

Mobapad Chitu 2 HD Silent Edition. In HLPLANET's spec table (Snimtas, 2026-05-21), every button that uses a microswitch on the standard model uses liquid silicone rubber on the Silent Edition. That covers ABXY, D-pad, triggers, bumpers and +/−. The sticks also glide on silicone tracks instead of hitting a hard plastic ring, with “almost no sound at all when you move the sticks”. No other pad here deals with stick-ring knock. HLPLANET calls it “one of the quietest controllers you can get (and maybe even the quietest overall)”. The trade-off: the D-pad cap is fixed. {buy:mobapad-chitu-2-hd-silent-edition}

EasySMX X05 Pro. EasySMX says its buttons use “restructured mechanics and silicone dampening” but does not list which ones. The same listing calls the D-pad “redesigned with tactile microswitch precision”. Two named ear tests split. Eric Hauter (Gaming Nexus, 2025-11-14) found the face buttons “not loud, but nothing special” with a small “pop”. He found the triggers, bumpers and D-pad “extraordinarily quiet”, and called it “definitely the quietest” of his many controllers. Liam Squires-Hand (GamingOnLinux, 2025-11-10) found “every other button is pretty much a whisper” apart from the thumbstick clicks, and felt “a clear click” on the D-pad. He also hit a trigger fault where light presses read as full pulls, which he called “a complete deal-breaker”. It is still the cheapest controller here with a maker quiet claim. {buy:easysmx-x05-pro}

GameSir Super Nova. GameSir limits its claim to “silent ABXY buttons”. Its spec sheet lists a membrane D-pad, but it makes no quiet claim for the bumpers or triggers.

EasySMX S05 Pro. EasySMX promises “silicone-damped buttons” and a “smooth disc-pivot D-pad”, with Switch 2 wake-up and a dock. We have no named ear test for it yet. {buy:easysmx-s05-pro}

Turn the rumble down too. Quiet buttons don't help if the motors buzz against a desk. On PS5, Sony's controller settings have Vibration Intensity and Trigger Effect Intensity under Settings > Accessories > Controllers. Lower both to quiet the DualSense's motors and trigger effects.

Not recommended

EasySMX X05 (non-Pro) for quiet play. It looks like the X05 Pro and costs $29.99, $6.00 less, but EasySMX's listing makes no quiet-button claim for it. If silence is the reason you're buying, get the Pro.
